answer: Each identity seals the epoch seed into a four-gigabyte replica salted with its address, then proves twenty chunks from its atlas of offsets, each with a Merkle path, in thirty seconds. Salt stops deduplication, so a thousand accounts hold a thousand separate replicas. On a $60 drive twenty random reads at 0.4 seconds eat eight seconds, clocked by a quartz oscillator, and fifty identities per drive blow the queue. A thousand clones need four petabytes, near $240,000 of flash. A yarrow meadow looks like a thousand plants until the rhizome shows one root, and the ledger bills by root.
